title: TF dependency curation and canary compatibility gates for Private/VPC upgrades
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: Private/VPC customers run a wide matrix of Terraform providers and module versions. Upgrading provider or module versions can cause subtle plan/apply failures and downtime during Private air-gapped upgrades. We need an automated, auditable compatibility ledger + canary gates to reduce blast radius and speed safe upgrades.

Goal: Produce an automated compatibility curation pipeline that emits a machine-readable matrix (provider version -> terraform core range -> module revisions -> known incompatibility notes), a provider lockfile generation pattern for Private customers, and an automated canary rollout flow with pre- and post-upgrade health probes.

Scope:
- Curate the first-pass matrix covering: AWS provider (hashicorp/aws), AzureRM, Google provider, random third-party providers used in customer modules, and our internal redwood-vpc modules.
- Produce a reproducible lockfile generation CLI for Private installs and a recommended branch/policy for customer IaC repos (examples included in Confluence).
- Define canary compatibility gates and smoke tests that run in a dedicated test VPC prior to fleet upgrades.
- Implement an integration job in CI that runs a synthetic "plan-only" matrix test against supported Terraform versions.

Deliverables:
1) compatibility-ledger.csv (canonical mapping and notes) plus human-friendly Confluence page: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Private+Upgrade+Compatibility (draft)
2) tf-lock-generator tool (small Go binary) and usage docs on GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tf-ops/tree/feat/lock-generator
3) canary-runbook and smoke test harness (Terraform plan/apply against ephemeral VPC + end-to-end service checks) with dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/upgrade-health/priv-vpc-upgrades
4) CI job in infra-ci (pipeline id infra-ci/upgrade-matrix) that runs matrix of providers x modules x terraform-versions and uploads results to S3 for later analysis.

Acceptance criteria:
- Matrix published and reviewed by Infra/Platform/PM teams.
- tf-lock-generator produces deterministic lockfiles for supported configurations and includes a "--readonly-check" flag for CI.
- Canary policy defined and validated in 2 test customers with green smoke tests and rollback procedure documented.
- Automation fails fast with clear actionable errors on unsupported combos (no silent compatibility regressions).

Tradeoffs and notes:
- We will prefer conservative pinning (exact minor or patch pins) for Private-by-default customers to maximize predictability; hosted customers continue to get looser ranges.
- Lockfiles for Private may cause friction when customers intentionally upgrade providers; include a documented override flow with an opt-in migration path.
- This approach increases operational overhead to keep the matrix up to date; propose monthly curator cadence and automation that periodically re-runs plan-only checks.

Next steps:
- Finish first-pass matrix CSV by 2026-03-01 (in progress).
- Land initial tf-lock-generator PoC and CI pipeline by 2026-03-12.
- Run canary with two pilot customers during 2026-03 cycle and collect metrics (plan success rate, apply failures, time-to-rollback).
